title: Questioning Binarity – Gender Diversity in Pain Medicine
summary: Current studies show clear differences in pain perception between cisgender women and men. The aim of this study is to investigate the role of gender and its various components on pain in healthy adults, with a particular focus on trans*gender people. This is done using standardized pain measurement methods and various questionnaires.
conditions: Gender-related differences in pain among cisgender and trans*gender individuals

interventions.name:
The study examines healthy subjects of different genders. This includes cisgender individuals as well as transgender and non-binary individuals (e.g., nonbinary, genderfluid, or agender).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
healthy
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, pre-existing conditions affecting pain perception, skin injuries on the back of the hand or forearm, regular use of painkillers, use of intoxicants 72 hours prior to testing.
